short: The first time human beings walked on another world, on 20 July 1969.
full:
Apollo 11's lunar module Eagle touched down in the Sea of Tranquility with about 25 seconds of fuel remaining, Neil Armstrong having taken manual control to avoid a boulder field. Armstrong stepped onto the surface some six hours later, followed by Buzz Aldrin; Michael Collins remained in orbit aboard Columbia.

The programme was a product of the Cold War — Kennedy's 1961 commitment was made after Gagarin's flight — and consumed about 4% of the US federal budget at its peak. Around 600 million people watched the landing live, the largest shared experience in history to that point. Twelve people have walked on the Moon; none since 1972.
